details:
I'm posting this in response to another canny post, to highlight my proposal for how to approach it. I think similar threads may have been posted before, but I want to stress the value here for solving a separate problem. A feature and a fix in one.

https://feedback.vrchat.com/feature-requests/p/tackle-the-misleading-world-thumbnails-issue

People dislike misleading thumbnails, whether AI or otherwise. They are becoming more and more common, used to obscure lower quality worlds and dishonestly lure visitors in.

I believe that adding the option for world authors to upload a few extra screenshots would go a surprisingly long way on helping with this issue.

Authors of high effort worlds that want to attract visitors and ensure their world isn't missed, are quite likely to take a minute to include extra screen shots to show it off.

Authors of low effort or otherwise basic worlds that hope to trick users into visiting, will either be forced to show the actual world with those screenshots, or won't be able to provide any. If they choose to use additional fake images then that will generally be much easier to notice, and would highlight the deception as being fully deliberate. Worlds that refuse to upload any additional shots despite having an amazing looking thumbnail, would be less trusted and less viral as a result.

Just this alone without even needing any potentially confidence sapping ratings, or any costly active moderation overhead, could likely solve the majority of the issue all on it's own.

It would allow honest authors to still use a fancy "splash page" if they like, whilst also demonstrating their world is legit and worth checking out. It wouldn't even need to be many extra images to function. A limit of somewhere around three to four images would be plenty for the proposed purpose.
title: Allow additional thumbnails for worlds - (To combat misleading thumbnails)
